¶2 Just a recap of what we said last week. The steps that mystic should take to come to the realization of l…….. in a manner which mistakes want to realize of the world, we mentioned that this was four steps that they have to take. The first thing was furbishing the body and soul with whatever Allah subhanaw taala has recommended us to do to the Prophet and this is called Tajliyah. And then the second step was after that there are issues in the heart which should be taken out the heart should be purified from evil and that is called takhliyah. And after that the soul could be adorned with the type of life which Allah (swt) wants to leave to to to a hardworking person.

¶3 And adorn this with knowledge with extra faith with the bonuses from the supernatural world and it is tahliyah which is adorning and then comes the position of fanaa or annihilation. Now, as you remember, we said that there were with regards to fanaa and also Baqaa was persistence and survival. There were different views, usually people who read about mysticism, they confuse the concept of annihilation or fanaa they think that people mystics they try to get to a position in which they lose their individuality. And there's nothing of them would remain, which of course, sounds not very reasonable. Therefore, we discuss about the different meanings given for fanaa and we mentioned that one of the best different definitions of fanaa, was given by Alexander Kynsh the Russian orientalist in his book Islamic mysticism, he says that there are two complimentary definitions of fanaa, one is passing away all things from the consciousness of the mystic, including self perception, so the the mystic would not see anything but God he doesn't even see himself.

¶4 He doesn't realize that there is an identity there as opposed to Allah subhanaw taala so he loses his old self perception, and this exponential vacuum is filled by a pure consciousness of God. In fact, he sees God and he doesn't see the creation. And in a metaphorical way, we could say that God would become a veil, which would cover him would not let him to see anything but him because now the glory of God is so great is heart, that they couldn't see anything beside, including themselves. So this is this is it is not an ontological, so to speak perception not something with regard to reality, but an epistemological issue. In fact, the knowledge of the mystic is tampered with sources the in a way that it cannot see they cannot see anything but God.

¶5 Now we cannot see anything but the creation we do not see God. The creation of the god is a vein, which will actually baar us from seeing Allah (swt). When they reached this the status of fanaa God Himself would become a vase for his creation so they couldn't see the creation anymore. They only see God and of course, this is this definition is complemented with another different definition which is falling away of the imperfect attributes of the fallible creature and their replacement by the purpose attributes of the Divine Self. Of course, you shouldn't think that this is the culmination and the end of this mystical journey. This is just the initiation of the mystic into the world of God in which at the beginning of this initiation there are so thrilled they are so excited.

¶6 So willed that they cannot see anything but God and this is what is called fanaa. Of course, as I said, there are other definitions of this experience by different people, but I think this is one of the best definitions that you can gather from what the mystics themselves said. In other words, as we mentioned last time fanaa is the annihilation of self perception of the mystic in perceiving the unveiling reality of God. Now, if you remember, we said that the whole idea of mysticism is to find out about reality in a way that they could sense they could taste it, this is what they call it tasty. They want to taste the reality. And this is the taste of it.

¶7 They now actually have the reality completely overwhelming, even their souls and there is nothing more pleasurable than this type of experience of reality. And of course, they do not experience reality in his wholeness because now they are barred from other parts of the reality. They only see the glory of God they go see his creation, and there is still a long way to go so that they could see both, creation and Allah subhanaw taala. And it is the annihilation of human characteristics of the mystic that would pave the way for attaining the attributes of gods. So, you see, to lose human characteristics it means that you have to lose your human ethos your human instincts your human drive, and by that we mean whatever evil in you should go away.

¶8 And when they go away, then it will pave the way for that knowledge and glory of God to fall and land into your heart. And that is what is called Fana. Nirvana is usually the concept of fanaa that we think about the destruction of the individuality. And Yahya Yathribi is the scholar of philosophy and mysticism in Iran? He writes on fanaa, that fanaa is not a negative process, as we usually think like Nirvana, but a positive one is breaking the lower limits and going to the higher stations.

¶70 Now, is there any question about fanaa and its degrees before we go to the next topic, which is of course quite related to this. No question. Okay, we move on. Now the Mystics say that the journey towards Allah subhanaw taala to be completed has four stages and that is what they call ‘al asfar al arbaat al ilahiyya’ the four divine journeys of the mystic. Actually, it's interesting that the philosopher Mulla Sadra has named his book of philosophy ‘al Asfaar e Arbaat’. And it's surprising because his book is of philosophy and he has put a mystical title on the book who knows why, anyone has any acquaintance with Mulla Sadra and why he has called his book asfaar e arbaat, while it is actually philosophy not mysticism because he himself claims that he has a rationalized mystcism.

¶71 He has brought all concepts which are only felt by experience by irrational experiences. He has rational all those with loss, ethical arguments, illustrations, as he has succeeded to great extent. And even some people say, Mulla Sadra horizon will be rationalized. Arabi speaks of his own experience in a way in a very wise way that he is not very worried about reason or rational arguments. But of course, Mulla Sadra has rational data and has that's why he has called him he has called his philosophy, not peripatetic philosophy neither elimination is philosophy which were the two branches of philosophy existed before him he has called it the transcendent philosophy and something. Now these four journeys of the mystic the first journey is the journey from creation to the haqq, and haqq means Allah (swt).

¶72 The second journey is the journey by haqq in the haqq and the third journey is the journey from the haqq back to the creation by haqq and the fourth is the journey in the creation by the haqq. Now what is the journey from creation to the haqq, okay, in this stage, the wayfare removes all the dark and the luminous veins from before his eyes or better say before his heart or her heart. The dark veils belong to the position of nafs, and the luminous stage belongs to the position of qalb and Ruhh, which are of course different layers of, of human soul. And I told you when you want to do something wrong and you tell yourself, don't do it is that position of your qalb, which talks to your nafs and says don’t do it, and that multifaceted type of being which is the magnificent creation of Allah subhanaw taala which works like instead it's created after his innocence can grow to the vicinity.

¶73 Now dark veils are the veils which are created by our own actions and we have created them during the course of the time. You remember in Dua Abu Hamza there is one very important trait which Imam Zainul aabedeen (as) said, you do not invade yourself from the creation. You are so shining so brilliant, so clear everyone can see you do not put yourself in veil. However, whatever they do, put themselves in a veil, whatever they do have veiled their hearts, they have created this dark layer on their heart and therefore they cannot see Allah (swt), this is the last verse. Now, then there are veils which are not created by our action but they are created by our existence because if these veils are taken away, of course, the whole creation would burn out.

¶74 We will perish from the glory of Allah (swt). So there are some veils put between him some buffers, so to speak, and the creation. Now in this journey, the wayfarer moves from the position of nafs, to the position of qalb, to the position of ruhh. The position of nafs is nafsul ammara which everyone has and the position of qalb is that nafsul lawwama and where the knowledge comes where the understanding comes. Inclusion of rule is the nafsul mutmainnah where the pure knowledge and pure lights come and this is the journey from creation to the haqq, the Journey culminates in Fanaa annihilation all the way, if they are successful if they can completely purify themselves, they come to that position where all the dark aspects of the soul go away and annihilation comes and they are at the end of the first journey towards Allah (swt).
